Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (SDK quickstart, auth, routing)

Hi Maria — thanks again for the call today, great context on the clinical ingestion flow. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can unblock the POC: 

What we covered
- Target workload: batched clinical notes -> embeddings -> reranker -> structured output (JSON tool-calling).
- SLA target: p95 latency < 350ms for single-record lookups; bulk embed workloads can be backgrounded.
- Security: you’ll use token-based service account keys + KMS for secret rotation.

Immediate next steps (recommended)
1) Try the attached quickstart-sdk-snippet.md — minimal Node and Python calls that use client-side streaming and backoff.
2) For auth, add a short-lived service token (rotate every 24h) and call our /v1/auth/validate endpoint to confirm scope.
3) Routing: start with the default region=us-fast; if you need lower cost we can route to the cpu-optimized pool for embeddings.
4) If you see 5xx errors during tool-calling, please capture a curl + full request/response headers and attach a repro.log — that helps us trace runtime errors quickly.

Notes on common gotchas (from similar customers)
- Structured tool-calling: send strict JSON schemas for arguments; malformed schemas often trigger a model runtime 500.
- Large batch payloads (>=1MB) can hit request size limits; split into smaller batches and use the /embeddings/batch endpoint.
- For rerankers: make sure the candidate set is <50 per query to keep latency predictable.

I've copied our engineers (Diego, Neha) on next steps if you want a joint debug session tomorrow.

Attachments: quickstart-sdk-snippet.md (small), sample-curl-requests.txt

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the repro, Maria — attaching quick notes from initial triage. I reproduced locally with the sanitized payload you sent. Summary: appears to be a structured-args parsing edge-case that triggers an unhandled exception in the tool-caller layer for the rwd-encode-1 model when the args object contains nested arrays mixed with null values.

Initial findings
- 500 stack shows JSON.parse on args failing where we call the tool schema validator (we use ajv). The validator threw a TypeError when encountering an array with trailing nulls in candidate metadata.
- Reproducer: I ran the same request against a local runtime and saw identical 500s at the tool-caller stage (before model call).

Immediate mitigation steps for the customer (to try now)
1) Trim the candidate set to <= 30 — fewer candidates avoid the edge path and reduces memory usage.
2) Ensure no nulls in nested candidate metadata (explicitly filter out nulls before sending). Example: candidates = candidates.filter(c => c != null).
3) Increase request timeout at the SDK client to 60s (default was 15s in their test) — shows as a hard fail instead of partial log capture.
4) As a fallback: set model_hint = "rwd-chat-compat" in the request to route to the chat-compatible variant that bypasses tool-caller validation for now.

Suggested dev action items (internal)
- Neha: can you add a defensive check in the tool-caller schema validator to coerce/truncate arrays that have trailing nulls? Ticket suggestion: INF-2219.
- Diego: I'll prepare a small regression test and a repro script we can share with Maria.

Sample SDK snippet to filter nulls (Node):
const filtered = candidates.filter(c => c !== null && c !== undefined);
await client.chat.create({ model: 'rwd-encode-1', input: { /* ... */, reranker: { candidates: filtered, top_k: 5 } } });

I’ll attach the repro script and a short runbook. If they still see 500s after trimming and timeout bump we should capture full server side logs for the timestamp in repro.log and escalate to runtime infra.

—Diego
